To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein–DNA binding is complex and that new DNA-binding specificites are encoded in multi-protein complexes.
DNA-binding specificity is achieved by a complex interplay between protein–DNA interactions, protein–protein interactions, DNA structure, DNA sequence and chromatin structure.
protein–DNA binding is complex at multiple levels and that multi-protein codes are a powerful mechanism for generating DNA-binding specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of DNA binding, and the impact of new technologies on our understanding of these mechanisms.
the complexities in protein-DNA binding and their impact on genome regulation and maintenance.
understanding the complexities of protein–DNA interactions and the multi-protein codes that underlie them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein–DNA recognition is complex and multifaceted, and that simple recognition codes do not exist.
the DNA-binding code is not simple.
there is no single, universal mechanism for protein–DNA recognition and that there are no universal rules for protein–DNA specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and applied a variety of new technologies for the characterization and analysis of protein–DNA interactions.
the DNA-binding specificity of proteins is encoded at multiple layers of complexity.

the complexities in protein-DNA binding are not just an inconvenience to be overcome, but a fundamental aspect of the process that has led to the evolution of sophisticated mechanisms of DNA recognition and regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA binding specificity of transcription factors and other DNA-binding proteins is encoded in a complex and multifaceted code that cannot be reduced to a simple recognition code.
DNA-binding specificity can only be fully understood by integrating data from multiple levels of the DNA-binding code.
DNA binding is complex, and the complexities are not easily reduced to simple rules.
